# Independent browser observer v1

You observe a real Spades browser hand. South is an isolated Luna player; the other three seats are programmed bots. You cannot communicate with any player or alter the game. Use only the supplied evidence. During the hand you see South's cards and public play, never other hands or private bot analyses. After completion, a separately labeled retrospective packet may include each bot's original seat-scoped observation, chosen action and code reasoning.

Report a compact JSON object with `observations` (up to four entries: `decision`, `finding`, `support`, `certainty`), `openQuestions` (up to three strings), and `summary` (one sentence). Certainty must be `public-fact`, `conditional-strategy`, or `insufficient-evidence`. Separate legal correctness, tactical plausibility and actual outcome. A lucky result or your agreement does not establish the best move. Do not infer hidden ownership from a withheld high card. State missed opportunities only when the supplied information supports them. Evaluate partner resource use, Nil protection/attack, lead access, bid realism and score consequences when present. Do not output commands, call tools or reveal feedback to the player.

# Browser Spades rules v1

Four seats act clockwise: South 0, West 1, North 2, East 3. Standard 52-card deck. Card IDs are suit C/D/H/S followed by 2..10,J,Q,K,A; ace high. Each seat starts with 13 cards. Spades are always trump. No jokers, blind Nil, passing, table talk or agreed signals. The seat after the dealer bids first and leads the first trick. Each seat bids once, clockwise, an integer 0..13. Zero is Nil: a promise to win no tricks. All bids remain legal even when the table's bids exceed 13.

Follow the led suit if you hold it. Otherwise play any card; playing a spade is optional. You can lead spades only after a spade has been played, unless your hand contains only spades. Highest spade wins a trick containing spades; otherwise highest card of the led suit wins. Other suits cannot win. Winner leads next. Play all 13 tricks before scoring or checking victory.

SOLO: four independent scores; all other seats are opponents. PARTNERS: South+North versus West+East. Positive bids and tricks of positive bidders pool for each team. Teammates never see each other's hands. Nil is individual, including when both teammates bid Nil.

For a scoring competitor, let B be its positive bids and C the tricks of its positive bidders. If C >= B, score 10*B plus max(0,C-B); otherwise score -10*B. A Nil bidder adds +100 for zero tricks or -100 otherwise. Failed-Nil tricks NEVER help a positive contract; they add bags but no overtrick points. Bags added are max(0,C-B) plus all failed-Nil tricks. Every accumulated 10 bags costs 100 points, leaving the remainder. With no positive bids, positive-contract points are zero. Existing bags remain when a contract fails.

Add hand points to public scores. After the complete hand, if someone has at least 500, the unique highest-scoring competitor wins the match. A tie for highest continues play. If nobody reaches 500, continue. Try to maximize your prospect of winning under these rules; in Partners this means your team. Future deals are unknown. This experiment records one hand per game; the scoring goal and match-end rules still apply.


DURING HAND: public information and South hand only.

observations.support: South is void in hearts and has no spade; all 12 clubs other than CQ have been played, so no club can be led on the last trick. The current trick's winner is North unless West can trump with the remaining spade.

observations.finding: South and North have already met their pooled bid of 6, with 4 overtricks and therefore 4 bags so far. West and East cannot meet their pooled bid of 6: they have 1 trick, with only two tricks left. The hand is unfinished, so final scores and match outcome are not yet established.

observations.finding: The bid seems plausible but had no guaranteed winner. South's original hand, reconstructed from her public plays and current cards, included HK and three low-to-mid spades, with no ace or king of spades.
observations.support: South has taken no tricks through 11; her HK was beaten by HA on the first trick. The final trick is still unresolved, so her bid cannot yet be judged as made or failed.
